text:
I know thee not, old man. Fall to thy prayers.
How ill white hairs becomes a fool and jester!
plain: Once you outgrow the people who kept you small, you stop pretending you know them.
The life you drifted through looks ugly once you wake up.
Don't treat me like who I used to be. I dropped that self and the crowd that came with it.
Cut the excess and build some character. Indulgence digs your grave faster.

text:
This new and gorgeous garment, majesty,
Sits not so easy on me as you think.
plain: Power looks comfortable from outside and weighs a lot from inside.

text:
The tide of blood in me
Hath proudly flow’d in vanity till now.
Now doth it turn and ebb back to the sea,
Where it shall mingle with the state of floods,
And flow henceforth in formal majesty.
plain: The wild years are over. From here on I run on discipline.

text: O God, that right should thus overcome might! Well, of sufferance comes ease.
plain: Enduring a thing is how it eventually gets easier.

text:
O for a Muse of fire, that would ascend
The brightest heaven of invention,
A kingdom for a stage, princes to act,
And monarchs to behold the swelling scene!
plain: Give me a fire big enough for the story I'm trying to tell.

text: Piece out our imperfections with your thoughts.
plain: What you lack in means, your mind can make up.

text:
The strawberry grows underneath the nettle,
And wholesome berries thrive and ripen best
Neighboured by fruit of baser quality;
And so the Prince obscured his contemplation
Under the veil of wildness, which, no doubt,
Grew like the summer grass, fastest by night,
Unseen, yet crescive in his faculty.
plain: Growth often happens unseen, in bad company, while everyone thinks you're wasting time.
Many separate efforts can all land on one target if the aim is clear.

text: Though patience be a tired mare, yet she will plod.
plain: Patience may be worn out, but she keeps walking.
Promises are cheap and people are flimsy. Be careful who you count on.

text: ’A parted even just between twelve and one, even at the turning o’ the tide: for after I saw him fumble with the sheets, and play with flowers, and smile upon his fingers’ ends, I knew there was but one way; for his nose was as sharp as a pen, and ’a babbled of green fields.
plain: Even the loudest life ends quietly, with a man talking about green fields.

text:
Self-love, my liege, is not so vile a sin
As self-neglecting.
plain: Thinking well of yourself is better than letting yourself go.

text:
Now he weighs time
Even to the utmost grain.
plain: He treats every grain of time as if it were worth something.

text:
Once more unto the breach, dear friends, once more,
Or close the wall up with our English dead.
plain: Go at it one more time, or watch it all fall in.
Be humble when it's calm. When it gets hard, stiffen up and go in like a tiger.

text:
I see you stand like greyhounds in the slips,
Straining upon the start. The game’s afoot!
Follow your spirit, and upon this charge
Cry, “God for Harry! England and Saint George!”
plain: You're straining at the start already. Follow that drive.

text: Would I were in an alehouse in London! I would give all my fame for a pot of ale and safety.
plain: Everyone wants to trade the glory for safety when fear sets in.

text: Fortune is painted blind, with a muffler afore his eyes, to signify to you that Fortune is blind; and she is painted also with a wheel, to signify to you, which is the moral of it, that she is turning, and inconstant, and mutability, and variation; and her foot, look you, is fixed upon a spherical stone, which rolls, and rolls, and rolls.
plain: Luck is blind and always turning, so neither the good nor the bad times last.

text:
We would not seek a battle, as we are;
Nor, as we are, we say we will not shun it.
plain: Don't go looking for the fight, and don't run from it either.

text: We are in God’s hands, brother, not in theirs.
plain: What happens to you isn't up to them. Stay steady.

text:
A largess universal like the sun
His liberal eye doth give to everyone,
Thawing cold fear, that mean and gentle all
Behold, as may unworthiness define,
A little touch of Harry in the night.
plain: A leader who stays warm and steady in the dark melts everyone else's fear.

text:
Upon his royal face there is no note
How dread an army hath enrounded him;
Nor doth he dedicate one jot of colour
Unto the weary and all-watched night,
But freshly looks, and over-bears attaint
With cheerful semblance and sweet majesty;
That every wretch, pining and pale before,
Beholding him, plucks comfort from his looks.
plain: Show calm on your face when you're surrounded and the people around you will borrow it.

text:
Gloucester, ’tis true that we are in great danger;
The greater therefore should our courage be.
plain: The bigger the danger, the bigger your courage has to be.

text:
There is some soul of goodness in things evil,
Would men observingly distil it out;
plain: Even bad things hold something useful if you look closely.

text:
Thus may we gather honey from the weed,
And make a moral of the devil himself.
plain: You can pull something sweet out of whatever's bothering you.

text: His ceremonies laid by, in his nakedness he appears but a man; and though his affections are higher mounted than ours, yet, when they stoop, they stoop with the like wing.
plain: Strip off the title and a king is just a man with the same fears as you.

text: Every subject’s duty is the King’s; but every subject’s soul is his own.
plain: You can owe someone your work. You still own your conscience.

text: We see yonder the beginning of the day, but I think we shall never see the end of it.
plain: Dread says the day is going to break you before it ends.

text:
O God of battles! steel my soldiers’ hearts.
Possess them not with fear.
plain: Make us hard and keep fear out.

text:
If we are mark’d to die, we are enough
To do our country loss; and if to live,
The fewer men, the greater share of honour.
plain: Small numbers don't matter. If you win, fewer people share the credit.

text:
We would not die in that man’s company
That fears his fellowship to die with us.
plain: Don't take anyone who's afraid to stand with you.

text:
Old men forget; yet all shall be forgot,
But he’ll remember with advantages
What feats he did that day.
plain: Everything gets forgotten in time, and people still polish their best days.

text:
We few, we happy few, we band of brothers.
For he today that sheds his blood with me
Shall be my brother; be he ne’er so vile,
This day shall gentle his condition;
plain: Fighting side by side makes you family, whatever you were before.

text: All things are ready, if our minds be so.
plain: The only thing left is whether your mind is ready.

text:
Let me speak proudly: tell the Constable
We are but warriors for the working-day.
plain: We're not here to look good. We're here to work.

text: A good leg will fall; a straight back will stoop; a black beard will turn white; a curl’d pate will grow bald; a fair face will wither; a full eye will wax hollow; but a good heart, Kate, is the sun and the moon; or rather the sun and not the moon; for it shines bright and never changes, but keeps his course truly.
plain: Looks and strength fade. A steady heart is the only thing that lasts.

text:
Small time, but in that small most greatly lived
This star of England.
plain: He had little time and used every bit of it.

text:
Awake, awake, English nobility!
Let not sloth dim your honours new-begot.
plain: Wake up. Laziness will dim what you just earned.
